title.source: 哆啦Ａ夢：作者走了30年，誰還在寫新故事？｜品牌故事
title.text: Doraemon: Who writes new stories, 30 years after its author died?｜Brand Story

description.source:
一張原稿留下來，新故事卻仍需要別人動筆。從むぎわらしんたろう另紙接續的回顧，追到2019年辻村深月與八鍬新之介處理月球資料、友情動機、台詞和小說化的工作，再讀2025、2026的版本署名。角色是虛構的，這份製作故事依當事人訪談與官方書目撰寫；匿名插圖不是歷史重建。

description.text:
An original manuscript survives, but new stories still need someone to write them. From Mugiwara's recollection of continuing on a separate sheet, we follow Tsujimura and Yakuwa's work on lunar research, friendship, dialogue and the 2019 novelization, then read the 2025 and 2026 credits. The characters are fictional. This production story uses participant interviews and official catalogues; anonymous illustrations are not historical reconstructions.

d1h011: 作者離世三十年後，你還能看到新的哆啦Ａ夢；
d1a021: 開場那支懸著的筆，讓我注意到一個很實際的選擇：
d1a033: 自己從《大雄的發條都市冒險記》連載第三回起接手。
d1a051: 那你在書店看到二〇一七年的《哆啦Ａ夢物語》，
是不是又有另一個接手年份？
d1a071: 《發條都市冒險記》的電影在一九九七年三月公開，
單行本在同年八月發售。
d1a081: 把這幾種日期分開，書架就好讀多了：
作品上映、整理成書、換成電子版，
d1a091: 但你可能還在等真正的難題：舊紙留下來了，
下一次遇到它上面沒有的新冒險，
d1b011: 替二〇一九年上映的《大雄的月球探測記》寫腳本時，
辻村深月收到むぎわら的鼓勵。
d1b031: 照辻村的說法，她因此開始把自己看成這一
次帶大家出發的人，能抬起頭寫台詞了。
d1b051: 如果換成你，要寫熟悉角色的新冒險，
最先找一個從沒聽過的王國，就能讓故事成立嗎？
d1b072: むぎわら在對談拿出舊構想便箋，
說自己以前也多次試過這個舞台，卻沒讓故事發展開。
d1c02b2: 要是得花很長時間解釋它怎麼運作，
觀眾可能還沒出發，就先被規則攔住了。
d1c02c3: むぎわら也談到，藤子先生善用圖解，
在少量格子裡讓孩子跟得上複雜概念。
d1c031: 辻村也說，她無法站在藤子先生的位置，
知道他會怎麼寫；可是長年讀這些角色，她能去想，
d1d031: 她原本會用長台詞交代情況和感受，
八鍬在幾個地方提醒她，聲優的表演加上畫面，
d1d061: 辻村還舉過一個例子：腳本只寫下神祕的月亮，
她還不知道它會是什麼顏色，
d1d082: 她起初沒立刻答應，問的是：
已經有漫畫和動畫，為什麼還要用小說來寫？
d1d101: 小說第一句寫到月球是人類難以生存的嚴酷世界時，
d1d112: 她形容，像是自己用小說再拍另一部電影，
從另一個角度進入同一個故事。
d1d122: 辻村說，原先以為已有畫面的部分會更快，
結果那些要自己從頭描寫的場面，
d1d12c2: 兒童文庫版會為漢字加上讀音，
她也就不刻意大量改用平假名；不懂的詞，
d1d131: 我覺得這才說明了，為什麼同一故事要重新署上寫作者：
媒介一換，就有人得重新選擇，
d1d14b1: 小說那年二月七日發售，電影三月一日上映；
書甚至比電影先到讀者手上。
d1d14b2: 你若把小說化一律想成電影上映後再找人抄寫，
這一版的時間順序就對不上了。
d1d151: 那你拿起漫畫形式的那一本，又能立刻認定，
是某位漫畫家重新手畫了整部故事嗎？
d1e011: 《月球探測記》這本全彩電影漫畫，
是用電影構成的漫畫形式，也就是動漫電影漫畫。
d1e012: 電影裡完成的影像，可以成為這種書的內容，
跟重新畫一套漫畫是不同工作。
d1e031: 所以你在書架上看到一個熟悉名字，
可以再多找一個欄位：這次是誰寫、誰畫，
d1e041: 那回到近年的電影，原作欄還在，
新腳本的作者是不是也一直固定同一個人？
d1e051: 二〇二五年的《大雄的繪畫世界物語》，
製作公司列導演寺本幸代、腳本伊藤公志。
d1e052: 同名小說再把伊藤列為著者兼腳本，
這一版的原作仍是藤子・Ｆ・不二雄。
d1e061: 到二〇二六年的《新大雄的海底鬼岩城》，
官方網站列的是導演矢嶋哲生、腳本村山功。
d1e07b2: 署名能帶你找到一份具體文本，
讓感興趣的人有機會往下追問，這一版到底怎麼寫。
d1e101: 哆啦Ａ夢的新故事，由各版本列名的創作者繼續寫，
原作署名則把這些新工作，
d1e121: 想繼續看熟悉名字背後，
真正讓作品往前走的人和工作，歡迎訂閱這個頻道。

lines.source: 作者離世三十年後，你還能看到新的哆啦Ａ夢；可是，只認「原作」兩個字，
lines.text: Thirty years after its author died, you can still see new Doraemon stories. But if you only notice the “original work” credit,

lines.source: 就可能看漏寫這一版故事的人。
lines.text: you may miss who wrote this version's story.

lines.source: 在留下來的原稿前，助手むぎわらしんたろう要接續大長篇，
lines.text: Facing the manuscript left behind, assistant Mugiwara was to continue the long-form manga,

lines.source: 卻沒有直接在那張紙上落筆。
lines.text: yet he did not draw directly on that sheet.

lines.source: 我在這裡先停了一下：要繼續畫，為什麼反而不碰原稿？
lines.text: I paused here: if he was going to keep drawing, why leave the original untouched?

lines.source: 後來，另一位導演帶著五、六本科學雜誌來開會；要讓熟悉的角色出發，
lines.text: Later, another director brought five or six science magazines to a meeting. To send the familiar characters on their way,

lines.source: 編劇先得面對月球上已經知道的事。
lines.text: the screenwriter first had to deal with what was already known about the Moon.

lines.source: 今天就沿著哆啦Ａ夢的創作工作，看看一張紙怎麼交到下一雙手。
lines.text: Today, let's follow Doraemon's creative work and see how a sheet of paper passes to the next pair of hands.

lines.source: 新故事到底是誰在寫，而一直留下來的原作署名，又承擔什麼工作？
lines.text: Who actually writes the new stories, and what does the enduring original-work credit do?

lines.source: むぎわら換了一張原稿紙，把先生的稿子轉寫過去，再接著工作。
lines.text: Mugiwara took a fresh sheet of manuscript paper, transferred his mentor's work onto it, then carried on.

lines.source: 照他在回憶書特設頁的署名留言，原來那份就這樣保留下來。
lines.text: According to his signed message on the memoir's special website, that preserved the original.

lines.source: 開場那支懸著的筆，讓我注意到一個很實際的選擇：你要完成眼前的作品，
lines.text: The hovering pen in the opening made me notice a practical choice: you can finish the work in front of you,

lines.source: 也可以替原件留出一個位置。
lines.text: and still leave a place for the original.

lines.source: 但接續到哪一回，能從這個動作判定嗎？
lines.text: But can that action tell us which installment he took over from?

lines.source: 這裡的先生，是本名藤本弘的藤子・Ｆ・不二雄。
lines.text: The mentor here is Fujiko F. Fujio, whose real surname was Fujimoto.

lines.source: 他在一九九六年九月二十三日過世。
lines.text: He died on September 23, 1996.

lines.source: むぎわら後來自述，自己從《大雄的發條都市冒險記》連載第三回起接手。
lines.text: Mugiwara later recalled taking over from the third serialized installment of Nobita's Clockwork City Adventure.

lines.source: 這次查到的是他的事後回憶，還不能憑它確定每一頁的作畫分工。
lines.text: What we found is his later recollection. It cannot establish who drew every page.

lines.source: 那你在書店看到二〇一七年的《哆啦Ａ夢物語》，是不是又有另一個接手年份？
lines.text: So when you see Doraemon Story from 2017 in a bookshop, is that another year when someone took over?

lines.source: 二〇一七年八月出版的，是むぎわら寫的回憶漫畫，一百三十頁。
lines.text: Published in August 2017, it is Mugiwara's 130-page memoir manga.

lines.source: 出版社介紹它收錄信件、下繪等資料；那是回頭講述與展示材料的時間。
lines.text: The publisher says it includes letters and preliminary drawings. That date belongs to the retelling and presentation of those materials.

lines.source: 同一個故事，為什麼又能在書目上看到二〇一六年？
lines.text: Why does a catalogue also show 2016 for the same story?

lines.source: 《發條都市冒險記》的電影在一九九七年三月公開，單行本在同年八月發售。
lines.text: The Clockwork City Adventure film opened in March 1997, and the collected manga went on sale that August.

lines.source: 現今書目另有二〇一六年的電子配信日期。
lines.text: Today's catalogue also lists a 2016 digital release date.

lines.source: 把這幾種日期分開，書架就好讀多了：作品上映、整理成書、換成電子版，
lines.text: Separate those dates and the shelf becomes easier to read: a film release, a collected edition and a digital edition

lines.source: 各自可以發生在不同時間。
lines.text: can each happen at different times.

lines.source: 書變新，不會讓當年的創作時間跟著往後移。
lines.text: A new edition does not move the original creative work to a later year.

lines.source: 但你可能還在等真正的難題：舊紙留下來了，下一次遇到它上面沒有的新冒險，
lines.text: But you may still be waiting for the real difficulty: the old sheet is preserved. When a new adventure is not on that page,

lines.source: 誰來決定角色往哪裡走？
lines.text: who decides where the characters go?

lines.source: 替二〇一九年上映的《大雄的月球探測記》寫腳本時，辻村深月收到むぎわら的鼓勵。
lines.text: While writing the screenplay for Nobita's Chronicle of the Moon Exploration, released in 2019, Tsujimura received encouragement from Mugiwara.

lines.source: 她在訪談裡說，那是一封電子郵件。
lines.text: In an interview, she said it came in an email.

lines.source: 她當時反覆想的是：自己可以替這些角色寫台詞嗎？
lines.text: She kept asking herself: was she allowed to write dialogue for these characters?

lines.source: 她轉述，信裡請她享受這次電影工作，想像角色也正期待新的冒險。
lines.text: She recalled the email inviting her to enjoy working on the film and imagine the characters looking forward to another adventure.

lines.source: 照辻村的說法，她因此開始把自己看成這一次帶大家出發的人，能抬起頭寫台詞了。
lines.text: According to Tsujimura, she began to see herself as the person taking everyone on this journey, and could write their dialogue with her head held high.

lines.source: 我覺得這裡很有意思：接過原稿的人，又幫另一位作者開工。
lines.text: I find this interesting: the person who took over the manuscript helped another writer get started.

lines.source: むぎわら在這一版還提供過有限的角色設計協助，也讀過最終腳本。
lines.text: Mugiwara also gave limited help with character design on this version and read the final screenplay.

lines.source: 如果換成你，要寫熟悉角色的新冒險，最先找一個從沒聽過的王國，就能讓故事成立嗎？
lines.text: If you were writing a new adventure for familiar characters, would picking a kingdom no one had heard of be enough to make the story work?

lines.source: 辻村先選的是月球。
lines.text: Tsujimura chose the Moon first.

lines.source: 她想讓觀眾走出戲院，再抬頭看月亮時，覺得那個地方比昨天親近一些。
lines.text: She wanted viewers leaving the cinema to look up at the Moon and feel it was a little closer than the day before.

lines.source: 可是月球也太熟悉了。
lines.text: But the Moon was almost too familiar.

lines.source: むぎわら在對談拿出舊構想便箋，說自己以前也多次試過這個舞台，卻沒讓故事發展開。
lines.text: During their discussion, Mugiwara brought out old idea notes. He said he had tried that setting several times before but could not get the story going.

lines.source: 觀測越多，能隨意安排的空間越少。
lines.text: The more we observe, the less room there is to invent freely.

lines.source: 開場那五、六本科學雜誌，就是八鍬新之介導演在首次討論時帶來的。
lines.text: Those five or six science magazines in the opening were what director Yakuwa brought to their first discussion.

lines.source: 辻村回顧，那次會議用科學資料討論設定；結果，寫腳本還是遇到困難。
lines.text: Tsujimura recalled discussing the setting with scientific material at that meeting. Even so, writing the screenplay was difficult.

lines.source: 你看，資料在這裡變成了寫作的阻力，也讓舞台有了邊界。
lines.text: You see, the research became an obstacle to writing, while also giving the setting boundaries.

lines.source: 要是只把月球當一塊空白背景，隨手放進王國，這次選它的理由就薄了。
lines.text: If the Moon were just a blank backdrop for any kingdom, the reason for choosing it would become weaker.

lines.source: 人已經想出發，資料也攤開了，但入口還沒找到。
lines.text: The writer wanted to set out, and the research was on the table, but the way in was still missing.

lines.source: 要怎麼讓原作的世界，真的接上這個新舞台？
lines.text: How could the original work's world really connect to this new setting?

lines.source: 八鍬提議，從原作短篇裡借一件已有的道具，讓大雄開始冒險。
lines.text: Yakuwa suggested borrowing an existing gadget from an original short manga story to start Nobita's adventure.

lines.source: 辻村回顧，聽到這個提議，故事才一下子動了起來。
lines.text: Tsujimura recalled that this suggestion suddenly got the story moving.

lines.source: 但你把舊設定拿來，就能用嗎？
lines.text: But can you simply take an old premise and use it?

lines.source: 要是得花很長時間解釋它怎麼運作，觀眾可能還沒出發，就先被規則攔住了。
lines.text: If explaining how it works takes too long, the rules may stop viewers before the adventure even begins.

lines.source: 辻村說，原短篇已經透過大雄的體驗，用幾頁把那件道具解釋清楚，
lines.text: Tsujimura said the original short story had already explained the gadget in a few pages through Nobita's experience,

lines.source: 她才有辦法把它放進電影。
lines.text: which made it possible for her to bring it into the film.

lines.source: むぎわら也談到，藤子先生善用圖解，在少量格子裡讓孩子跟得上複雜概念。
lines.text: Mugiwara also discussed how Fujiko used diagrams to help children follow complex ideas in just a few panels.

lines.source: 所以借到的不只是設定的名字，還有一個把設定講懂的方法。
lines.text: So they borrowed more than the name of a premise. They also borrowed a way of making it understandable.

lines.source: 至於角色該怎麼說話呢？
lines.text: And how should the characters speak?

lines.source: 辻村也說，她無法站在藤子先生的位置，知道他會怎麼寫；可是長年讀這些角色，她能去想，
lines.text: Tsujimura also said she could not stand in Fujiko's place and know what he would write. But after years of reading these characters, she could imagine

lines.source: 這個角色會說什麼、那個角色會採取什麼行動。
lines.text: what one character would say and what another would do.

lines.source: 我喜歡她把這兩件事分開。
lines.text: I like that she separates those two things.

lines.source: 導演怎麼檢查，這份冒險的動機寫得夠不夠？
lines.text: How did the director check whether the adventure's motivation was strong enough?

lines.source: 辻村說，八鍬要求她交代冒險理由，以及路卡對大雄的意義。
lines.text: Tsujimura said Yakuwa asked her to explain the reason for the adventure and what Luka meant to Nobita.

lines.source: 不能只靠「朋友」這個稱呼帶過。
lines.text: Calling him a “friend” was not enough.

lines.source: 她承認，一開始把為剛認識的客串角色努力，當成理所當然。
lines.text: She admitted initially taking it for granted that they would make an effort for a guest character they had just met.

lines.source: 這些追問讓她改從大雄和路卡這一對人物的關係，去思考動機。
lines.text: Those questions made her consider the motivation through Nobita and Luka's particular relationship.

lines.source: 想到角色關係的細節，電影腳本能像小說一樣一直加長嗎？
lines.text: As you work out those relationships, can a film screenplay keep growing like a novel?

lines.source: 辻村在有限的稿量裡安排台詞，得面對電影的時長。
lines.text: Tsujimura had to fit dialogue into a limited script length and face the film's running time.

lines.source: 她說，小說的篇幅可以自己決定，電影卻更要求台詞有效、節奏夠快。
lines.text: She said she could decide a novel's length herself, while a film demanded more effective dialogue and a quicker pace.

lines.source: 如果你在小說裡多留一段，讀者可以停下來慢慢讀；換成電影，
lines.text: If you leave an extra passage in a novel, readers can stop and take their time. In a film,

lines.source: 這段話就佔住所有觀眾同一段時間。
lines.text: those words take up the same stretch of time for every viewer.

lines.source: 我很好奇，她會怎麼處理那些長台詞？
lines.text: I wonder how she would handle those long speeches.

lines.source: 她原本會用長台詞交代情況和感受，八鍬在幾個地方提醒她，聲優的表演加上畫面，
lines.text: She had used long speeches to explain circumstances and feelings. At several points, Yakuwa reminded her that the voice actors' performances and the images

lines.source: 就足以傳達，只留下較短的一句便可以。
lines.text: could convey them, leaving just a shorter line.

lines.source: 辻村還舉過一個例子：腳本只寫下神祕的月亮，她還不知道它會是什麼顏色，
lines.text: Tsujimura gave another example: the script said only “a mysterious moon.” She did not yet know what color it would be,

lines.source: 動畫團隊卻能把那個月亮做出來。
lines.text: but the animation team could bring that moon into being.

lines.source: 文字交出去了，電影就算完成了嗎？
lines.text: Once the words are handed over, is the film finished?

lines.source: 她說，腳本完成後，導演和工作人員還要繼續大約一年半製作電影。
lines.text: She said the director and crew would continue making the film for about a year and a half after the screenplay was complete.

lines.source: 所以你看到的成片，還包含那些接著把文字變成影像的人所做的事。
lines.text: So the finished film you see also contains the work of the people who turned those words into images.

lines.source: 就在寫腳本期間，藤子プロ又邀她寫同一故事的小說。
lines.text: While she was writing the screenplay, Fujiko Pro also invited her to write a novel of the same story.

lines.source: 她起初沒立刻答應，問的是：已經有漫畫和動畫，為什麼還要用小說來寫？
lines.text: She did not agree immediately. She asked: with manga and animation already available, why tell it as a novel too?

lines.source: 如果只把電影裡說過的話抄一次，你也可能問，這本書多了什麼？
lines.text: If it merely copied what the film said, you might also ask what the book adds.

lines.source: 她得找出文字本身能接的工作。
lines.text: She had to find the work that words themselves could do.

lines.source: 小說第一句寫到月球是人類難以生存的嚴酷世界時，她發現，這跟腳本不同。
lines.text: When the novel's first sentence described the Moon as a harsh world where humans struggle to survive, she realized this was different from a screenplay.

lines.source: 場景、描寫、甚至演出的方式，都能在文字裡由她自己安排。
lines.text: She could arrange the settings, descriptions and even the way scenes played out herself, through words.

lines.source: 剛剛能交給動畫團隊的顏色與景象，現在得回到她筆下。
lines.text: The colors and sights she could hand over to the animation team now had to return to her pen.

lines.source: 她形容，像是自己用小說再拍另一部電影，從另一個角度進入同一個故事。
lines.text: She described it as making another film herself through a novel, entering the same story from a different angle.

lines.source: 再寫一遍，速度也會跟著變嗎？
lines.text: Would writing it again change her writing speed too?

lines.source: 她也寫角色當時的感受，還寫電影沒有的場景。
lines.text: She also wrote the characters' feelings at those moments, and scenes absent from the film.

lines.source: 辻村說，原先以為已有畫面的部分會更快，結果那些要自己從頭描寫的場面，
lines.text: Tsujimura said she had expected passages with existing images to go faster. Instead, the scenes she had to describe from scratch

lines.source: 反而寫得更有速度。
lines.text: were the ones she wrote more quickly.

lines.source: 那寫給孩子，就得把用詞全部變簡單嗎？
lines.text: And when writing for children, must you make all the vocabulary simpler?

lines.source: 到了這裡，辻村又得替讀者作一次選擇。
lines.text: Here, Tsujimura had another choice to make for her readers.

lines.source: 她說，自己後來不再一直按年齡區分讀者，希望大人孩子都能讀。
lines.text: She said she later stopped constantly separating readers by age and hoped both adults and children could read it.

lines.source: 兒童文庫版會為漢字加上讀音，她也就不刻意大量改用平假名；不懂的詞，
lines.text: The children's paperback edition adds pronunciation guides to kanji, so she did not deliberately replace lots of them with hiragana. Unfamiliar words

lines.source: 可以從前後文猜意思。
lines.text: could be understood from context.

lines.source: 我覺得這才說明了，為什麼同一故事要重新署上寫作者：媒介一換，就有人得重新選擇，
lines.text: I think this explains why the same story needs a fresh writer credit: when the medium changes, someone must choose again

lines.source: 用什麼方法讓你感覺到它。
lines.text: how to make you experience it.

lines.source: 新出的小說，總是等電影先上映嗎？
lines.text: Does a new novel always wait for the film to open?

lines.source: 二〇一九年的小說，出版社分列原作藤子・Ｆ・不二雄、著者辻村深月。
lines.text: For the 2019 novel, the publisher lists Fujiko F. Fujio for the original work and Tsujimura as the author.

lines.source: 同一部電影，另外還有一本全彩的電影漫畫。
lines.text: There is also a separate full-color film comic of the same movie.

lines.source: 小說那年二月七日發售，電影三月一日上映；書甚至比電影先到讀者手上。
lines.text: The novel went on sale on February 7 that year; the film opened on March 1. The book reached readers before the film.

lines.source: 你若把小說化一律想成電影上映後再找人抄寫，這一版的時間順序就對不上了。
lines.text: If you assume every novelization is someone copying a film after its release, this version's dates do not fit.

lines.source: 那你拿起漫畫形式的那一本，又能立刻認定，是某位漫畫家重新手畫了整部故事嗎？
lines.text: And when you pick up the comic-format book, can you immediately assume a manga artist redrew the whole story by hand?

lines.source: 《月球探測記》這本全彩電影漫畫，是用電影構成的漫畫形式，也就是動漫電影漫畫。
lines.text: The full-color Moon Exploration film comic is a comic assembled from the film: an anime film comic.

lines.source: 電影裡完成的影像，可以成為這種書的內容，跟重新畫一套漫畫是不同工作。
lines.text: The film's completed images can become the contents of such a book. That is different work from drawing a new manga.

lines.source: 換看《大雄的新恐龍》的漫畫版，出版社就分列：
lines.text: Look instead at the manga version of Nobita's New Dinosaur, and the publisher separates the credits:

lines.source: 原作藤子・Ｆ・不二雄、腳本川村元氣、漫畫むぎわらしんたろう。
lines.text: original work by Fujiko F. Fujio, screenplay by Kawamura, manga by Mugiwara.

lines.source: 這一列把寫腳本和畫漫畫的工作攤開了。
lines.text: That line lays out the work of writing the screenplay and drawing the manga.

lines.source: 所以你在書架上看到一個熟悉名字，可以再多找一個欄位：這次是誰寫、誰畫，
lines.text: So when you see a familiar name on a shelf, you can look for another field: who wrote it, who drew it,

lines.source: 還是把電影整理成書？
lines.text: or was the film assembled into a book?

lines.source: 我現在看這些署名，會先找版本，再找工作。
lines.text: When I read these credits now, I find the version first, then the work.

lines.source: 那回到近年的電影，原作欄還在，新腳本的作者是不是也一直固定同一個人？
lines.text: Back with recent films, the original-work credit remains. But has the new screenwriter always been the same person?

lines.source: 二〇二五年的《大雄的繪畫世界物語》，製作公司列導演寺本幸代、腳本伊藤公志。
lines.text: For 2025's Nobita's Art World Tales, the production company lists Teramoto as director and Ito as screenwriter.

lines.source: 同名小說再把伊藤列為著者兼腳本，這一版的原作仍是藤子・Ｆ・不二雄。
lines.text: The novel of the same name also lists Ito as both author and screenwriter. This version's original work is still credited to Fujiko F. Fujio.

lines.source: 到二〇二六年的《新大雄的海底鬼岩城》，官方網站列的是導演矢嶋哲生、腳本村山功。
lines.text: For 2026's New Nobita and the Undersea Devil's Castle, the official site lists Yajima as director and Murayama as screenwriter.

lines.source: 新一版換了具體工作的人，原作欄仍保留藤子先生。
lines.text: The people doing particular jobs change in a new version, while Fujiko remains in the original-work field.

lines.source: 但「新的腳本」，就一定是從沒出現過的故事嗎？
lines.text: But does a “new screenplay” necessarily mean a story that has never appeared before?

lines.source: 而且這次連回一九八三年的作品，是把大長篇再拍成電影。
lines.text: This one also returns to a 1983 work, adapting a long-form manga into a film again.

lines.source: 新的腳本署名，可以出現在舊故事的新改編裡，
lines.text: A new screenplay credit can appear on a new adaptation of an old story,

lines.source: 不能光靠上映年份判斷故事是不是首次出現。
lines.text: so the release year alone cannot tell you whether the story is appearing for the first time.

lines.source: 這一版豪華碟片的附件介紹，還列出村山功一百六十頁的縮印腳本。
lines.text: The deluxe disc edition's extras also list a 160-page reduced-size printing of Murayama's screenplay.

lines.source: 署名能帶你找到一份具體文本，讓感興趣的人有機會往下追問，這一版到底怎麼寫。
lines.text: A credit can lead you to a specific text, giving interested readers a chance to ask how this version was written.

lines.source: 那官網列出的公司名字，能直接告訴你，誰寫了這個腳本嗎？
lines.text: And can the company names on the official site directly tell you who wrote that screenplay?

lines.source: 同一份二〇二六年官網，也列出製作單位和東寶配給。
lines.text: The same 2026 official site also lists the production organizations and Toho as distributor.

lines.source: 這些欄位回答誰參與製作、誰負責配給；找誰寫這份劇本，得讀腳本欄。
lines.text: Those fields tell you who participated in production and who handled distribution. To find the writer of this screenplay, read the screenplay field.

lines.source: 我喜歡那個另取一張紙的動作。
lines.text: I like that action of taking a fresh sheet of paper.

lines.source: 保存讓過去的工作有跡可循，接續的人則得面對今天的新問題。
lines.text: Preservation leaves a trail of past work, while those continuing it face today's new problems.

lines.source: 哆啦Ａ夢的新故事，由各版本列名的創作者繼續寫，原作署名則把這些新工作，
lines.text: Doraemon's new stories continue through the creators credited on each version. The original-work credit connects that new work

lines.source: 連回藤子・Ｆ・不二雄創造的世界。
lines.text: back to the world Fujiko F. Fujio created.

lines.source: 熟悉的故事換人寫，你最希望保留什麼，願意在留言裡說說嗎？
lines.text: When someone new writes a familiar story, what would you most like to keep? Would you share it in the comments?

lines.source: 想繼續看熟悉名字背後，真正讓作品往前走的人和工作，歡迎訂閱這個頻道。
lines.text: To keep finding the people and work behind familiar names that really move the stories forward, subscribe to this channel.
